analysis:
The UPA's Common Minimum Programme, adopted in May 2004, listed as its first economic objective ensuring that the economy grows at least 7-8% per year in a sustained manner over a decade and more, with employment generation.

Independent compilations of official data put average real GDP growth for 2004-05 to 2013-14 at about 7.6% (UPA-I 8.0%, UPA-II 7.0%). That falls inside the 7-8% band the CMP set, although annual growth was uneven, ranging from about 9% in some years to under 5% in 2012-13 and 2013-14.

The promise is measured on the stated metric (average growth over the period), not on the employment condition attached to it; employment growth over the period was a separate and more contested question.
notes: The CMP is a UPA document; it is attributed here to the Prime Minister who led the UPA government. Growth figures are at factor cost on the 2004-05 series; the EPW table was consulted via search-result text, not the full PDF. No unverified YouTube video was cited.
